title: ✈️ Telegram celebrates its thirteenth birthday… welcome messages and interactive buttons inside messages!
body: ✈️ Telegram celebrates its thirteenth birthday… welcome messages and interactive buttons inside messages!
Telegram has launched a new update for its thirteenth birthday, adding new tools for group and channel owners, developers, and users.
Group and channel owners can now create welcome messages for new members, reaching them the moment they join.
Developers can add interactive buttons to messages and build temporary experiences inside the chat itself, without leaving the app.
The rich text editor now supports documents, files, and music inside messages, turning a single message into a content-rich card.

The update also added signatures and comments for collectible gifts bought through the Telegram marketplace, and a placeholder element that helps users update old versions of the app when they cannot display the new features.
This update comes days after another major update on November 20 that added a news bar and AI agents inside the app.
Simply put: Telegram is turning a message from plain text into an interactive space: automatic welcomes for members, buttons that open experiences, and files and music inside the conversation itself.
Would you rather messaging apps stay simple, or do these additions make them better?
